ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Article L561-1 et seq. and Article L561-45 et seq. of the French Code monétaire et financier (CMF); Article L223-1 et seq. of the Code de commerce (SARL rules); Décret n°2016-1637 of 28 November 2016 on registers of beneficial owners; AMF General Regulation; and the transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) into French law, as amended by Décret n°2020-1123 of 4 September 2020. The UBO declaration must be filed simultaneously with the registration of the company at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the INPI Guichet Unique.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government trade register / company registry of the parent company's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if applicable)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and continuous screening of all managers, shareholders, and beneficial owners against (1) the French national list of persons subject to asset-freezing measures published by the Direction générale du Trésor (DG Trésor); (2) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list (EU regime); (3) the United Nations Security Council consolidated list; (4) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for any USD-denominated wire transfers; and (5) domestic PEP databases covering public officeholders, their family members and close associates. Screening is required before incorporation, before funds wiring, and subsequently on a risk-based rolling basis. Any positive hit automatically triggers enhanced due diligence, immediate reporting to TRACFIN (the French FIU), and freezing of assets.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises — operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), via https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (branded as 'Procédures INPI')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company's dénomination sociale must be written in Latin script and may include French words, registered trademarks, or ordinary expressions. If the name includes non-Latin characters (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic), a mandatory transliteration into Latin alphabet must be included in the constitutional documents. The corporate name must include the legal form indicator 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.À.R.L.' and must be available under Article L711-2 et seq. of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle. Official statutory documents, contracts, invoices, and all communications with French administrative authorities must be in the French language, except where an official opposed language is permitted by EU law.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the INPI portal rejects a name reservation, the applicant receives a written or electronic statement of reasons. The applicant may submit a formal administrative reconsideration request (recours gracieux) to the Director General of INPI within one month of notification, attaching corrected name proposals and legal argumentation. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal before the competent administrative court (Tribunal administratif de Paris) within two months of the negative decision. Where rejection is based on prior trademark or company-name rights, the applicant may alternatively seek an amicable coexistence agreement or a transfer of the conflicting asset before initiating judicial affects. The name reservation can be renewed by refiling after the 30-day expiry; no statutory extension exists beyond the initial reservation term.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or domiciliation office is permissible for a French SARL, but only through a licensed 'société de domiciliation' registered with the local préfecture. The domiciliation agreement must be formalized in writing and the address must be geolocated in France and used exclusively for the company's registered office (siège social). For an electric passenger bus OEM, virtual office use is acceptable only for the early holding phase; actual manufacturing, customs clearance, and bid participation require a physical establishment with substantial local substance. If the company claims the title 'manufacturer' under ISIC 2910 and applies for municipal contracts, it must maintain a physical facility where buses are assembled and tested. Any virtual office that does not reflect genuine management and operational substance will expose the company to corporate tax re-domestication by the DGFiP under Article 211 of the Code général des impôts and to sanctions for artificial arrangement under France's domestic GAAR (L'Avis de l'Administration).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections is elevated for a newly formed manufacturing company seeking municipal EV procurement contracts. The DGFiP, URSSAF, and French regional customs authorities maintain a coordinated inspection program; the probability of a physical inspection during the first 12 months is estimated at 35–45% for ordinary manufacturing establishments, rising to 55–70% when the company registers for VAT and applies for municipal green procurement tenders, and an additional 20–30% higher if the company relies solely on a virtual office. Inspection priority is determined by risk scoring, including use of a domiciliation address without visible production capacity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-2, L.223-1 through L.223-43 (SARL), R.123-1 et seq. (RCS); Décret n° 2022-725 of 28 April 2022 (guichet unique); Code de l'environnement for industrial site permits.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office; centralized electronic filing through the INPI 'Guichet unique' portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M 'Création d'entreprise' plus the signed Articles of Association (statuts) and supporting annexes, transmitted electronically through the Guichet unique; registration is evidenced by a Kbis extract (extrait d'immatriculation au RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required by French law for a SARL. The Articles of Association fix the capital amount. Cash contributions must be fully paid at incorporation and held in a blocked account at a bank, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or before a notary; the funds are released to the manager only after presentation of the RCS/Kbis registration certificate. Contributions in kind must be assessed in the Articles and transferred in full.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The initial members of [Company Name], a French SARL, (1) approve the Articles of Association; (2) subscribe in full the share capital of EUR 10,000, as 10,000 ordinary shares of EUR 1.00 each; (3) confirm cash contributions are deposited in a blocked account, to be released after RCS registration; (4) adopt the registered office at [Address] within the jurisdiction of [Commercial Court]; (5) appoint [Name] as first gérant with full power to represent, sign, and manage the company; and (6) authorize the gérant to publish the legal notice, file at the Guichet unique, and to take every action required for incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the Articles of Association and corporate governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders, legal counsel, and, if a contribution in kind is engaged, a notary; notarization is mandatory where real estate or certain assets are contributed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French-language statuts containing corporate name, legal form SARL, duration (maximum 99 years), corporate purpose (manufacture, assembly, distribution, and maintenance of pure electric municipal transit buses and shuttles), registered office address, share capital breakdown, cash/kind contributions, rights attached to shares, first manager's identity, and governance rules. The founders must initial every page, sign the final deed (sous seing privé) or notarial deed (acte notarié) if any contribution involves real property. Keep identical executed originals for all signatories and the registry file.
required_dossiers: Valid identity document or passport of each member
Proof of domicile or nationality details
Draft Articles of Association
General meeting delegation/power of attorney where a founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry later queries a statutory clause, the members may execute an amending resolution (décision collective) correcting the clause; the corrected document is refiled through the Guichet unique before the court denies registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Block capital contributions and obtain the bank's certificate of deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank chosen by the founders or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC); the account must be opened in the future company's name.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the bank with the project statuts and the list of contributors. Transfer the total cash contribution into a blocked account held in the name of the company being formed. Request the attestation de blocage des fonds / certificat de dépôt des fonds, specifying the amount and the blocked nature. The bank releases the funds only against presentation of the Kbis extract and a mandate from the first manager.
required_dossiers: Project Articles of Association
Identity documents of the manager or authorised representative
List of shareholders and subscribed shares
Proof of transfer of cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate due to a mismatch in the statuts, correct the statuts and resubmit; if the bank delays, engage another bank or the CDC and request a formal blocking certificate before progressing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the mandatory legal notice in an authorized legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorised in the department of the registered office; published online or through the official service providers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a concise notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, first manager, and the RCS court with which registration is sought. Submit the notice to the JAL and pay the publication fee. Obtain the attestation de parution and preserve the original gazette page or digital proof for the registry filing.
required_dossiers: Notice text prepared in French
Proof of payment of publication fees
Reference copy of the project Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains a typographical or legal inconsistency, publish a corrective notice (avis rectificatif) in the same JAL and submit the rectification to the registry; failure to publish invalidates the registration train and must be cured before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the incorporation dossier through the Guichet unique and pay registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI's Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's jurisdiction, acting as the RCS registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the official French business formalities portal. Select 'Création d'entreprise' and the legal form SARL. Complete the mandatory administrative form M, attach the statuts as a PDF, upload the bank certificate, legal announcement attestation, proof of office address, manager identity and consent, declaration of non-conviction, declaration of beneficial owner, and any power of attorney. Verify all fields, pay the non-taxable registry fee online, and submit. Keep the electronic filing receipt (dépôt). The registry verifies legal compliance and the absence of conflict with public order.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed statutory form M
Signed Articles of Association (full text)
Bank certificate of blocked capital or notarial attestation
Legal announcement attestation from the JAL
Proof of authorization to use the registered office address
Identity document and residential proof of the first manager
Sworn declaration of absence of judicial conviction applicable to the manager
Beneficial owner declaration (titulaire effectif)
Power of attorney if the filing is made through a professional authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet unique or registry issues a request for complementary documents or a draft refusal, respond electronically within the prescribed period (generally 15 working days) by uploading missing documents. If a definitive refusal is issued, the applicants may exercise a gracieux appeal to the President of the Commercial Court or file a substantive remedy before the competent court to force registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Kbis extract and complete post-registration social and fiscal formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE (SIREN/SIRET); URSSAF and tax authorities triggered by the SARE/auto-registration procedure.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registry validates the incorporation, the Greffe issues the official Kbis extract containing the RCS number, SIREN, SIRET, legal capacity date, registered office, managers, and corporate object. The company obtains legal personality from the registration date. Download or order additional authenticated copies for banks, municipal procurement files, and contractual counterparties. If employees are hired, register the company as an employer with URSSAF, obtain the CICE-related declarations and register on the professional healthcare/caisses system within the applicable deadlines. Publish the incorporation mention in BODACC automatically.
required_dossiers: Registration validation receipt
Official Kbis request form
Copy of approved statuts and registry file delivery acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance is delayed, request an urgent delivery order from the Greffe; if Kbis contains data errors, file an omission/rectification request before the Greffe and, if unresolved, before the judge supervising the registry of commerce and companies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), Inspection des Installations Classées (ICPE); local Préfecture for authorization decisions; CARSAT for occupational risk clearance and DREETS for workplace regulatory controls.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE operating permit / registration certificate / declaration receipt for the electric bus manufacturing and assembly facility, issued according to the applicable ICPE classification rubrics of the French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement, Livre V, Titre I), completed by any required planning permission (permis de construire) and urbanism authorization for the industrial plant.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires; DREAL as the territorial authority; INERIS may be consulted as technical support for hazard and impact studies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: The site is normally subject to DREAL 'Enregistrement' (Category 2) for a medium-scale vehicle assembly operation with surface coating and metal working activities. If the production capacity crosses thresholds imposing higher foreseeable pollution or hazard, the facility falls into 'Autorisation' (Category 1) requiring a full environmental impact assessment (étude d'impact) and public inquiry. Small sub-threshold facilities may qualify for non-ICPE or simple declaration status after site-specific classification review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the general ICPE ministerial order of 2 February 1998: pH 5.5-8.5, temperature <30°C, suspended matter ≤30 mg/L, BOD5 ≤30 mg/L, COD ≤125 mg/L, and no hydrocarbons above 10 mg/L unless stricter site-specific Prefect limits apply. Air emissions and VOC thresholds must respect Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions and the applicable best available techniques; solvent-containing finishing installations must meet total organic carbon/VOC mass flow limits set by the Prefect in the operating permit. All industrial waste must be tracked using the bordereau de suivi de déchets (BSD) and registered in the waste register, with disposal only through licensed carriers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety engineering: the plant must obtain a fire safety certificate from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) or a recognized inspection body, covering fire compartments, egress routes, extinguishing systems, and dangerous substance storage. Structural load and stability certification, based on a building inspection and the planning permission, is required for the assembly hall, roof, mezzanine, and bus lifts. Occupational clearance under the French Labour Code: installation must be designed following the occupational health and safety rules, CARSAT inspection, and DREETS validation of machine guarding, electrical installations, chemical risk assessment (document unique), ventilation, and emergency-response plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL obtains SIREN and SIRET from INSEE; foreign entities with taxable presence register for TIN/VAT ID through DGFiP procedures including PE declaration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch elections governed by EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturation électronique with real-time reporting to tax authorities via API for all VAT-registered entities

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT on exports of goods to non-EU countries or offshore services; eligibility requires proof of export and non-EU destination
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of delivery
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Clawback of zero-rated VAT with penalties up to 80% of the tax amount plus interest; fraudulent claims may result in criminal prosecution

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange, balance-of-payments, and international financial statistics are administered principally through Banque de France and the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a euro-area jurisdiction with a freely convertible currency and no general exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions. The SARL may receive foreign capital, pay foreign suppliers, repatriate dividends, repay documented shareholder loans, and convert euros into other currencies, subject to corporate-law approvals, distributable-profit rules, withholding-tax analysis, transfer-pricing requirements, anti-money-laundering controls, sanctions screening, beneficial-ownership verification, and applicable balance-of-payments reporting. Dividend distributions require approved annual accounts and legally distributable reserves. Payments to related non-residents must be supported by arm's-length documentation. Foreign direct investment screening may apply to acquisitions or investments in protected strategic activities; ordinary electric-bus manufacturing is not automatically subject to screening, but activities involving critical technologies, defense, energy, transport infrastructure, data, or other protected interests require a case-specific assessment under French investment-control rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a French bank, convert export receipts into euros, or maintain a prescribed foreign-currency conversion ratio. Export proceeds may remain in foreign-currency accounts, subject to the bank's account terms, AML controls, accounting requirements, and tax rules. There is no general mandatory statutory deadline for conversion of export receipts. Banks may request commercial invoices, customs evidence, transport documents, contracts, and payment-purpose information. Banque de France or the relevant reporting institution may require balance-of-payments or statistical reporting for qualifying cross-border transactions. Cash and certain payment instruments transported across EU external borders are subject to applicable EU and French cash-control declarations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. and its relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne network institution

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment accounts and operational collections; low as a substitute for a full-service French relationship bank. An EU-authorised electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide euro payment accounts, SEPA transfers, foreign-exchange services, and certain card or collection products under its home-state authorisation and passporting framework. It may not be treated as a bank for all purposes, cannot provide bank deposits unless separately authorised, and customer funds are generally safeguarded rather than covered by the French deposit-guarantee regime. Offshore or non-EEA digital EMIs require appropriate local authorisation or passporting and may face correspondent-bank, safeguarding, sanctions, AML, tax-residency, and French IBAN acceptance constraints. A fintech account should not be the sole account for capital escrow, high-value industrial trade, payroll, public-sector collections, or complex LC activity without written confirmation of product capability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available using qualified electronic identification, certified corporate documents, video identification, and beneficial-owner verification. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting or live video interview for non-resident managers, complex ownership chains, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual payment flows, capital escrow release, cash-intensive activity, or unresolved source-of-funds questions. The account-opening package should identify the manager or legally authorised representative, ultimate beneficial owners, signatories, tax residencies, expected transaction profile, and governing powers. A French registered office, valid SIREN/SIRET registration, articles of association, Kbis extract, and evidence of business substance materially improve onboarding viability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent SARL incorporation records, missing Kbis extract, unregistered registered office, or mismatch between articles, beneficial-owner filing, bank mandate, and commercial-register data.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; signed articles of association; certificate of incorporation or registration evidence; registered-office lease or domiciliation agreement; beneficial-owner declaration; manager appointment evidence; board or shareholder resolutions; bank mandate; identity and address evidence for managers, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident ownership, nominee shareholders, layered holding companies, trusts, bearer-like arrangements, or inability to identify natural-person ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart to natural persons; certificates of incorporation and registers of shareholders and directors for each intermediate entity; notarised or certified ownership documents where requested; trust or foundation instruments; beneficial-owner attestations; tax-residency certificates; explanation of control rights; sanctions and politically exposed person screening records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, shareholder loans, acquisition funding, or large inbound transfers inconsistent with the stated business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital subscription documents; shareholder-loan agreement; investor bank statements; audited accounts; sale-of-business or financing documents; tax filings; proof of accumulated wealth where relevant; remitter-to-shareholder relationship evidence; transaction purpose letter; expected-flow schedule; bank confirmation of originating account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border payments involving new suppliers, intermediaries, freight agents, distributors, or jurisdictions subject to sanctions, corruption, export-control, or enhanced AML scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed purchase and sales contracts; supplier and customer due-diligence files; invoices; purchase orders; bills of lading or transport documents; customs declarations; end-use and end-user statements; sanctions-screening results; beneficial-owner checks; anti-bribery certifications; commission agreements; proof of delivery; documented escalation and approval controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Electric-vehicle manufacturing, battery, dual-use, public-procurement, or municipal-customer exposure creating perceived export-control, strategic-sector, or corruption risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product classification and technical specifications; battery and component origin records; export-control assessment; end-use certificates; procurement tender documents; municipal-counterparty verification; anti-corruption policy; conflict-of-interest declarations; distributor due diligence; environmental and product-compliance registrations; evidence that no restricted military or sanctioned end use is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected activity materially exceeds the stated profile, including large FX conversions, cash deposits, third-party payments, rapid pass-through transactions, or payments unrelated to bus manufacturing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial model; monthly cash-flow forecast; contract pipeline; production and procurement plan; payroll estimate; customs and logistics forecast; expected countries and currencies; payment-volume matrix; treasury policy; segregation-of-duties controls; explanation of seasonality and one-off capital expenditure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, CRS, FATCA, or beneficial-owner information inconsistencies, including foreign managers or investors with incomplete self-certifications.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax-identification evidence; CRS self-certifications; FATCA forms where applicable; foreign tax-residency certificates; entity classification memorandum; investor and manager identification documents; explanation of dual residency or controlling-person status; updated corporate tax and VAT registrations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital and shareholder loans from an account held in the documented name of the investor or lender to the SARL's French bank account using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-euro payments. Use a clear payment reference identifying capital contribution, capital increase, or shareholder loan and the relevant agreement. Provide the bank with the subscription agreement, shareholder resolution, amended articles where applicable, capital-deposit certificate requirements, loan agreement, source-of-funds evidence, ownership chart, and remitter verification before settlement. For a new SARL, capital may be deposited into a blocked capital account with an authorised French bank or other legally permitted depositary and released after registration evidence is supplied. Record the transaction in the statutory accounts and reconcile it to the share-capital or shareholder-loan ledger. Apply EU and French sanctions, AML, tax, transfer-pricing, foreign-investment-screening, and statistical-reporting checks. Do not use unexplained third-party remitters, personal accounts, cash, or informal netting arrangements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments to EEA beneficiaries, subject to bank limits and fraud controls. Use SWIFT cross-border transfers, normally MT103 or the current ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or non-euro payments; retain the payment instruction, purpose, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, contract, and sanctions-screening records. For high-value or documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit, preferably an irrevocable documentary credit subject to UCP 600, issued or confirmed by a bank acceptable to the beneficiary and supported by compliant invoices, transport documents, insurance documents, certificates of origin, inspection documents, and required customs or export-control records. A standby letter of credit or demand guarantee may be used where commercially appropriate under ISP98 or URDG 758. Municipal or public-sector customers commonly pay through procurement-contract and bank-transfer mechanisms rather than a letter of credit; confirm the tender, budget, guarantee, invoicing, acceptance, and public-payment requirements before relying on LC proceeds. Prohibit split invoices, false descriptions, third-party settlement, sanctions-evasion routing, and payment against incomplete shipping or end-use documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and other bank-quoted FX forwards for forecast or contracted receivables and payables, documented under an ISDA or bank master agreement where required and supported by an underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for hedging committed or recurring multi-currency funding and liquidity exposures, subject to counterparty credit, collateral, valuation, accounting, and EMIR requirements.
FX options, collars, and participating forwards for defined commercial exposures, subject to suitability, product-governance, valuation, disclosure, and accounting controls.

Non-deliverable forwards only for currencies or jurisdictions where deliverable conversion is restricted or commercially unavailable, provided the instrument is offered by an authorised counterparty, the reference currency and settlement mechanics are documented, sanctions and local-law restrictions are cleared, and the hedge is linked to a genuine underlying exposure.

Spot FX conversions for settlement and liquidity management. Speculative dealing unrelated to identified commercial, financing, or balance-sheet exposures should be prohibited under the treasury policy.

For an EU corporate using derivatives, assess EMIR clearing, reporting, margin, risk-mitigation, collateral, portfolio-reconciliation, and financial-counterparty classification requirements; maintain hedge documentation consistent with IFRS 9 or the applicable French accounting framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting (AGE) — approval of annual statutory financial statements and appropriation of profit or loss
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records — registre des délibérations des associés at registered office; no external authority filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months following fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager civil liability for loss caused by failure to convene; any shareholder may petition the commercial court to appoint a temporary agent to hold the meeting (C. com. art. L.223-27).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements, management report and shareholders' resolutions with the Trade and Companies Register (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce du siège social (via INPI/RCS teleprocedure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the annual general meeting; approval must occur no later than six months after year-end, therefore not later than seven months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court may order filing under coercive penalty (astreinte); any interested party may request designation of a court-appointed agent; repeated non-filing may lead to administrative strike-off from the RCS (radiation).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats no. 2065-SD) with supporting schedules and balance of corporate income tax (solde d'impôt sur les sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end: 3 May by EDI (paper deadline 19 May in official calendar practice); for staggered year-end: within three months of the balance-sheet closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of net tax due (40% after formal notice, 80% for abusive scheme); late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; fixed penalty for each omitted schedule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax compliance — Contribution Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) payment and, where applicable, declaration of new or modified business premises (form 1447-C)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP — local public finance offices and the municipal tax centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Full payment by 15 December of the tax year; where annual amount exceeds EUR 3,000, two equal instalments due 15 June and 15 December; form 1447-C by 31 March for new or restructured establishments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest plus 10% penalty under Article 1727 of the General Tax Code; under-declaration may lead to an increased taxable base and a 5% administrative surcharge on instalments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner register (RBE) accuracy review and any necessary modification declaration after share transfers or control changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via INPI/RCS teleprocedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following any change in ultimate beneficial owners; where there is no change, no annual re-declaration is required by French law but verification is performed at the time of annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted beneficial-owner statements expose the manager to fines up to EUR 15,000 and possible imprisonment; company directors may additionally be barred from managing commercial activities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) for a SARL when, at the close of a fiscal year and during the preceding year, two of the following three thresholds are exceeded: total balance sheet assets above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory where the company controls or is controlled by entities exceeding the thresholds, or upon a shareholder request holding at least one-tenth of the share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles (Plan Comptable Général — PCG) under Articles L.123-12 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements but not for the statutory individual accounts of a SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: French law does not impose a standalone annual UBO re-declaration. The RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) is updated only upon actual changes in beneficial ownership, with a filing due within 30 days of any share transfer or change in control. At the annual general meeting, the gérant must verify that the register of share transfers, the register of associates, and the RBE data accurately reflect current ownership; any discovered discrepancy must be rectified by an INPI/RBE filing. A statement of confirmation may be recorded in the minutes but not filed separately with the greffe.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share transfers (registre des mouvements de titres)
Shareholders' decision minute book (registre des délibérations des associés)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150 - 700 per year for a third-party commercial registered office domiciliation in French metropolitan jurisdictions
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 20,000 - 50,000 for a mid-size electric bus OEM subject to the compulsory statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, with the balance taxed at 25%, if their paid-up capital is fully paid and at least 75% owned by individuals or qualifying entities and their annual turnover, excluding tax, does not exceed EUR 10 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% reduced rate is subject to the conditions stated above. Eligible research and development expenditure may qualify for the French research tax credit (crédit d'impôt recherche, CIR), generally at 30% up to EUR 100 million of eligible expenditure and 5% above that amount, subject to statutory eligibility and filing requirements. Other incentives may apply only if the company satisfies their specific statutory conditions; no general tax holiday applies to ordinary bus manufacturing.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to an annual deduction cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The portion not deductible in a year remains available for later years. A limited one-year carryback election may be available, subject to statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), filed electronically through the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) professional tax portal, impots.gouv.fr, using EDI-TDFC or the applicable online procedure. The return is accompanied by the applicable tax and accounting schedules, generally forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD under the régime réel normal, or forms 2033-A-SD to 2033-G-SD under the régime simplifié.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; four corporate income tax instalments may be payable during the financial year, subject to statutory exemptions and thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. For a financial year ending on 31 December, it is due by the second working day following 1 May, subject to any officially announced electronic-filing extension. The corporate income tax balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally 15 May. Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to applicable rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SARL's legal name, SIREN number, registered address, tax office, activity, accounting period, and applicable tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned French SARL reports its French entity details and French taxable results. A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the SARL as the corporate taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD — corporate income tax regime and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable profit or loss, applicable rate, tax credits, instalments, tax due, and any balance or credit. Reconcile accounting profit to taxable profit through the required schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income taxable in France at the SARL level. Apply treaty relief, where relevant, to a separately identified cross-border payment; do not omit French-source income merely because the shareholder is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the balance sheet, income statement, fixed-asset and depreciation details, provisions, tax adjustments, and other schedules required by the SARL's accounting regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose related-party balances and transactions accurately and retain supporting accounting records in accordance with French law. Use the applicable French statutory accounting and tax classifications.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD — tax credits and incentive claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible credits, including the CIR where applicable, and submit required supporting forms and declarations within their respective deadlines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not itself qualify the SARL for an incentive. The French SARL must satisfy the relevant substantive, documentation, and filing conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD — corporate income tax balance payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronically report and pay the corporate income tax balance, or report an overpayment, using the DGFiP professional portal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is the French SARL's responsibility regardless of the residence of its shareholders. Maintain a French-compatible electronic payment arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and pay required instalments on the statutory quarterly dates, calculated under the applicable prior-year tax rules and exceptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess instalment obligations at the SARL level; do not assume that foreign ownership or a first operating year automatically removes payment obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after formal notice where the return remains unfiled, and potentially 80% in cases such as discovery of an undeclared activity. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge plus late-payment interest, ordinarily 0.20% per month, subject to statutory exceptions and adjustments. Understatement may trigger additional surcharges, commonly 40% for deliberate breach and 80% for fraud or specified abusive conduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French SARL to a non-resident, the domestic withholding tax rate is generally 25% for a corporate recipient, subject to treaty relief and domestic exemptions. A qualifying EU parent company may obtain an exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive and French implementing rules, generally requiring a qualifying participation, holding period, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse compliance. Rates and treatment for individual recipients differ.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, determine the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, participation, and eligibility under the applicable France tax treaty and domestic anti-abuse provisions. Obtain a current tax residence certificate from the competent foreign tax authority. Submit the applicable French treaty-relief certificate, commonly form 5000-SD and, for dividends where applicable, form 5001-SD, through the payer or withholding agent under the relevant procedure. The payer should retain the certificate and supporting evidence. Where relief is not obtained at source, the recipient may generally seek a refund using the prescribed forms and evidence, subject to the applicable claim deadline. Treaty relief is not automatic and may be denied under anti-abuse or principal-purpose rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident are generally subject to French withholding tax at the domestic corporate rate, generally 25%, subject to an applicable treaty rate or qualifying EU exemption. Interest paid to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, except notably where statutory exceptions apply, including payments to recipients in non-cooperative jurisdictions; treaty rules and anti-abuse provisions must be checked. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and payment type. Confirm beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, debt characterization, deductibility, and any EU directive conditions before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150 million turnover or gross assets, generally, for a French entity or French tax group within the statutory scope, including specified ownership or control relationships; the threshold and scope must be tested under the rules applicable to the relevant fiscal year. French companies subject to the documentation requirement must prepare Master File and Local File documentation and provide it to the tax authorities upon request. A separate annual transfer-pricing summary declaration (form 2257-SD) may be required for entities meeting the applicable statutory criteria. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations as a separate general regime. French transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, permanent-establishment, anti-abuse, and general anti-avoidance rules require transactions and arrangements to reflect their actual functions, assets, risks, decision-making, and commercial purpose. A low-substance French entity may face challenges to treaty benefits, deductions, profit allocation, or the existence and characterization of its activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing bus sales, components, engineering, management services, royalties, guarantees, or financing outside the arm's-length range; failing to maintain required documentation; or deducting interest contrary to French limitation rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable-profit adjustments, late-payment interest, and applicable tax surcharges. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may result in a penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 5% of the transfer-pricing adjustments, subject to statutory rules and caps.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director is not automatically liable for company tax debts. Personal liability may arise under statutory conditions for fraudulent conduct, serious and repeated tax-law breaches, or insolvency-related misconduct; criminal tax fraud can result in individual fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax fraud and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable receipts, using false invoices, knowingly misstating costs or tax credits, maintaining hidden accounts, or arranging sham transactions to evade tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, and surcharges that may reach 80% in specified cases. Tax fraud may be prosecuted criminally; individuals may face imprisonment and fines under the applicable provisions of the French Tax Code and Penal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally participate in, direct, or knowingly facilitate fraud may face criminal prosecution and personal penalties. Civil tax liability may be imposed on a director only where statutory conditions are met; imprisonment is not an automatic consequence of a company tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared permanent establishment or disguised French activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a French office, personnel, dependent agent, or other fixed place to conduct taxable activity while omitting required registration, returns, or French-source profit attribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of French corporate income tax, applicable withholding taxes, VAT and related liabilities, interest, and penalties. Treaty protection depends on the relevant treaty facts and cannot be assumed from the absence of a French subsidiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal exposure depends on individual participation and statutory grounds, including tax fraud or insolvency misconduct; foreign residence does not itself eliminate potential French enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend, royalty, or interest withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a treaty rate or exemption without valid residence and beneficial-ownership evidence, failing to withhold, or mischaracterizing a distribution as deductible interest or royalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French payer may be liable for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable surcharges. Treaty relief may be denied where anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, or principal-purpose requirements are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may face personal consequences where the statutory conditions for fraudulent conduct, personal participation, or tax-debt liability are satisfied; liability is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to trade while insolvent, diverting assets, preferring related parties, failing to file for insolvency proceedings when legally required, or distributing assets to shareholders to defeat creditors or tax claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil and commercial consequences may include repayment, asset recovery, management bans, and liability for all or part of an insufficiency of assets where statutory conditions are met. Criminal sanctions may apply to specified bankruptcy offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face personal civil liability, management prohibitions, or criminal prosecution for qualifying misconduct. Travel bans are not a standard automatic sanction for ordinary tax non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing proceeds of crime, concealing beneficial ownership, making prohibited payments, or breaching applicable EU or French financial sanctions in municipal procurement, import, or cross-border payment activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences depend on the offence and may include asset freezing, transaction prohibition, regulatory or criminal fines, and imprisonment. Applicable sanctions screening and reporting duties must be assessed for the transaction and counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who authorize, facilitate, or knowingly participate in unlawful conduct may face personal criminal or regulatory liability. Corporate status does not shield an individual from liability for personal involvement.
